title: Type hierarchy on a page — Image Wiki

rules.rule: If a page uses only one type size, it will appear as a wall where readers cannot visually distinguish the order of information without reading every line.
rules.evidence: Left, one size, one leading, no gaps: a wall. You can read it, but you cannot see it — finding the address means reading every line until you hit it.

rules.rule: If a page uses only type size to create hierarchy, it will feel busier and more insistent than using space or weight.
rules.evidence: Right, no gaps at all, but five type sizes doing the separating. It works too, and notice what it feels like: busier, more insistent, and the small last line has been pushed toward the illegible.

rules.rule: If a page uses only one type size with empty lines between groups, it will create four visible parts without changing the rhythm or requiring extra type sizes.
rules.evidence: Middle, still one size everywhere. The only change is empty lines between the groups, and now the page has four visible parts.
